title: Fine water mist and orientation-independent discharge
summary: A NASA technical brief reports a proof-of-concept water-mist design that extinguished open and baffled-enclosure fires and discharged in different orientations.
designImplication: Research extinguisher access, enclosure penetration, recharge resources and compatibility with breathing protection together.
limitations: The cited equipment result is not a PSI solid-fuel test row or a universal extinguishment guarantee.
Agent dose, droplet distribution, enclosure, ventilation, fuel and electrical compatibility need application-specific qualification.

title: Smoke-property coverage for advanced detection
summary: SAME reports material-dependent smoke distributions; a single average particle size can hide a substantial larger-particle mass fraction.
designImplication: Build a detector validation matrix across aerosol size, material, airflow and aging, including representative pre-fire heating products.
limitations: Smoke-property findings do not establish detector sensitivity, false-alarm rate or alarm time for a particular habitat.
NASA describes possible use in submarines and underwater laboratories; this is an application prospect, not a deployment claim.

title: Material screening across atmospheres and gravity
summary: NASA combustion studies connect material selection with oxygen, ventilation, geometry and gravity rather than treating flammability as a material-only label.
designImplication: Export exact material, shape, thickness, oxygen, pressure and flow metadata before comparing test outcomes or training a model.
limitations: Small-sample or simulated-gravity findings do not certify a full cabin or Moon-surface installation.
An unmeasured condition combination remains a research gap even when its individual variables appear in separate tests.

title: Diagnostics beyond visible flame disappearance
summary: NASA reports cool-flame observations after hot-flame quenching; CFI-G uses faint-emission imaging and thermal information to investigate low-temperature chemistry.
designImplication: Separate visual observations from heat-release or chemical-state measurements when defining a research endpoint or model target.
limitations: Cool-flame observations are configuration-specific and are not a detector-selection or crew-response procedure.
Engine efficiency and emissions are research applications; an optimized terrestrial device is not delivered by this dashboard.

title: Electric fields for cleaner terrestrial combustion
summary: E-FIELD Flames investigates ion-driven flow, stability and soot control for efficient, lower-emission combustion.
designImplication: Compare field strength, ion current and flame response as research variables rather than treating electrical forcing as a ready fire extinguisher.
limitations: NASA explicitly states this experiment is not conducted to serve a space application.
No spacecraft suppression performance or electrical hardware qualification is inferred.

title: Soot and stabilization models for practical burners
summary: SPICE studies smoke-point behavior; SLICE studies flame attachment and liftoff to support combustion-model development.
designImplication: Keep fuel, nozzle, coflow and flame-state fields available so researchers can compare relevant configurations and model targets.
limitations: Shared hardware does not make the SPICE smoke point and SLICE liftoff threshold the same outcome.
Combustor-model relevance does not establish solid-material or smoke-detector performance.

title: From sample tests to cabin-scale fire monitoring
summary: Saffire provides a larger-spacecraft research setting that complements small samples and smoke-measurement investigations.
designImplication: Compare temperature, combustion-product sensing, ventilation and confinement before transferring a laboratory finding to a vehicle-level monitoring study.
limitations: Saffire flights have different configurations; a result from one is not a controlled replicate of another.
The dashboard informs equipment research and data collection, not installation approval or emergency response.

title: NASA technology heritage in firefighter protection
summary: NASA documents lightweight breathing-apparatus technology transfer and earlier flame-resistant protective-material development for firefighting.
designImplication: Use this as a documented technology-transfer example; assess modern protective-equipment requirements with the relevant current engineering evidence.
limitations: This broader NASA safety heritage is not represented as a result of BASS, FLEX, SAME or another PSI campaign.
Historical documentation does not establish the current certification or suitability of any product.
